questions.question: What is a shell structure? Give two natural and two human-made examples.
questions.expected_answer: A shell structure is hollow, with a strong outer covering that carries the load. Natural examples include eggs, snail shells, crab shells and tortoise shells. Human-made examples include helmets, buckets, cooldrink cans, car bodies and dome tents.

questions.question: Why is a crab's outer skeleton called a shell structure, and what jobs does it do?
questions.expected_answer: It is a hard, hollow covering on the outside of the body with the soft parts inside, so it is a shell structure. It supports the body, gives it shape, protects the soft parts and gives the muscles something to pull on.

questions.question: Explain how a crab grows, and compare a frame skeleton with a shell skeleton.
questions.expected_answer: Its hard shell cannot grow, so the crab moults: it climbs out of the old shell, swells up and its new soft shell hardens a size bigger. A frame skeleton inside can grow with the animal and allows large bodies; a shell skeleton outside gives all-round armour but must be moulted to grow.
